task.description: Read docs/agents/design/REQ-001a.md independently — not CODE-DESIGNER's result.summary. Run WF-02 Step 1b's full gate: (a) every acceptance criterion has a corresponding design element, no TBD/deferral language; (b) props/types fully specified; (c) every color/spacing/typography reference resolves to an actual token — note this project's real constraint (already established in WF-01's gate cycle) is that the switcher intentionally uses src/app/globals.css's bespoke classes, NOT docs/Design system for AI agents/tokens/tokens.css — verify the design doc cites globals.css correctly with accurate line numbers, not the documented design-system tokens path; (d) no implementation code present (no .tsx code blocks, structure/types only). Also specifically assess CODE-DESIGNER's flagged open question: it could not confirm whether Next.js 16 requires `proxy.ts` instead of `middleware.ts` (Next 16 deprecated middleware in favor of proxy per node_modules/next/dist/docs/.../file-conventions/{middleware,proxy}.md) since next-intl isn't installed yet to check its exact expected file/export name against Next 16. Decide: is this a legitimate open question to hand to FRONTEND-DEV to resolve during implementation (Step 2 agents can check next-intl's actual installed package/docs once it's added as a dependency), or does it need to block this gate? Read the actual Next.js 16 proxy/middleware docs yourself to inform this judgment.

result.summary: Read docs/agents/design/REQ-001a.md directly (not CODE-DESIGNER's handoff summary) and ran WF-02 Step 1b's gate against it. (a) Acceptance-criteria coverage: SS8's table maps every scope bullet (dependency, routing restructure, message catalogs, switcher, layout.tsx metadata, root redirect) to a concrete design section; the only 'not specified'/deferral language is confined to the explicitly labeled SS7 Open Questions, which is the correct location for genuine unknowns, not a dodge of a required element. No bare TBD found in the body sections. PASS. (b) Props/types: SS3 gives LocaleSwitcher's full signature (no props, self-contained via useLocale()/usePathname()), the internal Locale union type, and per-Link field-level detail (href/locale/className/text semantics); SS5 gives RootLayout's new signature (LayoutProps<"/[locale]">, async generateMetadata); SS6 gives routing.ts's field types. Field-level, not prose-only. PASS. (c) CSS verification: read src/app/globals.css directly. All cited line numbers are byte-accurate: header.nav 36-40, .nav-in 41, .brand/.brand img 42-44, .nav-links/.nav-links a/.nav-links a:hover 45-47, .lang 48-49, .lang span 50, .lang .on 51 all match the real file exactly. Confirmed :root (lines 1-11) uses bespoke hex/oklab vars, not design-system OKLCH tokens, and the doc never cites docs/Design system for AI agents/tokens/tokens.css for the switcher (only correctly notes it does NOT apply). PASS. (d) No implementation code: all code fences in the doc are a file tree, two JSON catalog samples, and one next.config.ts plugin-wrapper shape snippet (no JSX/component bodies, none tagged tsx/jsx). Matches doc's own SS8 claim. PASS. (e) proxy.ts/middleware.ts open question: read node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/middleware.md and proxy.md, and 01-app/01-getting-started/16-proxy.md directly. They confirm the design doc's SS0/SS7.1 claims precisely: middleware.js is deprecated in Next 16 and renamed to proxy.js, functionality/signature (NextRequest in, NextResponse out, same matcher shape) unchanged, version-history table confirms v16.0.0 as the deprecation version. The design doc's recommendation (create proxy.ts at project root, export default proxy wrapping next-intl's returned handler) is fully actionable now from primary Next.js docs; only the next-intl-package-specific detail (its own docs' exact expected export name once installed) is deferred, and that is unknowable before the dependency exists in node_modules. This is a correctly-scoped, legitimate open question for FRONTEND-DEV at Step 2, not a gate-blocking gap. Verdict: PASS, no rework required.
